info.title: Tenant API - Billing micro-service
info.description:
Settl Tenant API documentation

Current tenant APIs

The following is a list of available Tenant APIs in Settl, you can visit the documentation for each API by replacing the {BASEURL} with the url in your browser before :{PORT}/swagger

Production APIs

  • Market micro-service: {BASEURL}:4002/swagger/index.html?urls.primaryName=Tenant
    • The Market micro-service is responsible for handling market communication in DK,FI,NO,SE and maintaining master data for time series, electricity metering points, tariffs and more.
  • DebtorFinance micro-service: {BASEURL}:4059/swagger/index.html?urls.primaryName=Tenant
    • The DebtorFinance micro-service handles transfer of account vouchers to finance systems for bookkeeping.

APIs for testing only

  • Commodities micro-service: {BASEURL}:4031/swagger/index.html?urls.primaryName=Tenant
    • The Commodities micro-service contains metering points for any non-electricity commodity, as well as metering point related data like profile calculation.
  • Billing micro-service: {BASEURL}:4001/swagger/index.html?urls.primaryName=Tenant
    • The Billing micro-service manages master data related for billing entities within a tenant context.
      Customer Api: Queries for getting customer information.
      Payer Api: Queries for getting payer information.
      Contract Api: Queries for getting contract information.
      Product elements Api: Queries for getting product element information.
  • Invoicing micro-service: {BASEURL}:4043/swagger/index.html?urls.primaryName=Tenant
    • The Invoicing micro-service contains details about invoices generated by Settl, as well as endpoints to get the actual invoice (PDF).

General information

The Settl tenant API is a collection of REST APIs designed to allow Settl tenants to interface with the Settl billing solution for system to system integrations, data exports and similar.

The tenant APIs are provided with guarantees of backwards compatibility by using versioned endpoints which will only change according to the below definition of forward compatible changes.

If a change in the Settl system requires the tenant APIs to change in a way which breaks the API contract, a new version of the endpoint(s) will be released and tenants will by default be given a 6-month(*) deprecation warning to the existing endpoints.

Tenants are expected to switch to the new API versions within the 6-month period given, and the existing versions will be marked as obsolete.

(*) If special circumstances arise like legal or market changes which cannot be announced with a 6 month warning in advance, new API versions will be created and need to be adopted faster.

Version compatibility

The following changes to the API are considered non-breaking:
  • Adding JSON parameters to responses.
  • Adding optional parameters to requests.
  • Changing links that are returned in the response when calling the APIs. However, request parameters (i.e., query parameters) that the client supplies remain unaltered.
  • Adding new query parameters to a link that is handed out (i.e., the added query parameters become part of the link that is handed out). The clients should pay attention to this when adding "existing" query parameters they are used to supply.
  • Changes in page sizes returned when calling APIs with paging. The server determines the page size. The client follows the next and prev links to page through the result.
  • Changes to sorting unless the sorting is explicitly defined by the API endpoint.

Entity relationship

The data structures in the Settl market module is the related according to the below entity relation diagram, where the MeteringPoint is one main entry.
    
                        MeteringPoint
                       /     |   |    \
        MeteringGridArea     |   |     MarketPriceList
               /             |   |
          EnergyParty        |   MarketBalanceArea
                   \         |   |
                     \       |   |
                        TimeSeries
Any entity can be visited using the entity specific API endpoints, the relationship between the entities is controlled using properties associating from top level entity to a lower level entity. These properties will be named according to the entity they point to, postfixed with Id as the value of the property will always be a GUID reference to a specific instance of the entity pointed to.

Example:

A MeteringPoint will (optionally) be related to a MarketBalanceArea using the property MarketBalanceAreaId

Pagination

Any endpoint returning lists of data e.g. search operations, will by default use pagination. The Settl backend is configured with a maximum page size, and will only return elements up to that limit in one response. The response will always contain a url NextUri defining how to get the next page of elements. By visiting the NextUri continuously until it is null all elements from the search will be returned. A link pointing backwards to the previous page PreviousUri is also generated to make it easy to navigate back and forth through the pages. Notice: Searches are not guaranteed to return pages that are fully ordered. If data is created in the system while the search is being performed, it can influence the pages being returned, depending on the search filters and sorting options used.

Historical data

A number of entities in Settl are represented with different values for the data for different periods of time. This is very useful in a billing solution as it allows the system to represent how data was defined in the past, is currently defined, and might be defined in the future. E.g. a balance supplier is only the active supplier for a MeteringPoint while there is an active agreement with the customer/consumer. If another balance supplier makes an agreement to supply the consumer instead, Settl will receive this information and represent it as a future state for the InDelivery boolean flag in the metering point data. If data is historical, it will be grouped along with a time period definition showing at what times the data values should be used. The example below has two different values for the delivery status of the metering point: 
    
    "HistoricalDeliveryStatuses": [
    {
        "InDelivery": true,
        "End": "2023-12-31T23:00:00Z",
        "Start": "2022-12-31T23:00:00Z"
    },
    {
        "InDelivery": false,
        "End": "9999-12-31T23:59:58.999Z",
        "Start": "2023-12-31T23:00:00Z"
    }
    ]
The above data represents that the balance supplier (the tenant in this API context) using Settl has been delivering the supply for this metering point for all of 2023, and then the consumer/customer has ended the agreement.

Authorisation and access

Endpoints are protected using OAuth2/OIDC access tokens. To call an endpoint you must first retrieve an access token using a supplied clientId, clientSecret, username and password. The flow is a OIDC resource owner password flow. The following example shows how to retrieve an access token 
 
curl --location '{BASEURL}/security/connect/token' \
--header 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
--header 'Authorization: Basic {BASE64ENCODE}(ClientId:ClientSecret)' \
--data 'grant_type=password&username={USERNAME}&password={PASSWORD}&scope=BIO_Client+BIO_Api'
Notice the ":" in ClientId:ClientSecret and notice that OIDC is build into many toolkits directly so you might not need to code the above. Notice the string after "Basic" is a base64 encoded string of the client id and client secret combination. Notice If you are accessing the internal APIs leave out "/security" from the url and replace with the security micro-service port number :4003 You can choose to add a offline_access scope, but when used for system to system integration there is little reason. The returned access_token has a lifetime. There is no reason to fetch a new access token before the end of the lifetime. That only slows operations. Once you have extracted the access token from the response you can call the protected endpoint. For example 
    
curl --location '{BASEURL}/market/tenant-api/v1/metering-points' \
--header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
--header 'Accept: application/json' \
--header 'Authorization: Bearer [access-token]'
Notice: Because the endpoints are protected with authorization one cannot directly follow links from the responses in a browser unless you install additional plugins to add the bearer token to you browser headers.

API gateway

When Settl is deployed in a production configuration, another security layer is introduced. Azure API Management is used to control the access to the Settl backend. In this configuration any API call to the tenant APIs will have to go through API Management. An API base url will be provided from Settl to the API consumer, it is unique per Settl installation meaning it will be a different base url for e.g. test and production. An example base url: https://apim-settl-settldev-northeu.azure-api.net/ The Settl backend consists of a number of micro-services running as individual web APIs each with their own API endpoints. To access a specific set of tenant APIs, a "Settl service suffix" is needed in addition to the base url e.g. "market" or "security". A full example API call will then look like: https://apim-settl-settldev-northeu.azure-api.net/market/tenant-api/v1/metering-points where the endpoints defined in this OpenAPI/Swagger documents are the remaining part of the urls. A "Subscription key" is used to ensure that only allowed API consumers are forwarded to the Settl backend, this is a authorization key assigned to each API client, and which must be provided either as: * query parameter subscription-key=[subscription-key] * header --header 'Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key: [subscription-key]'

Data formats

  • Dates and DateTimes are in ISO8601 format and in UTC. Eg. 2023-05-28T14:00:00.00Z
  • Time periods are always "end exclusive" meaning the End timestamp of the period is not part of the period. The period ends right before this time stamp. As such two directly consecutive time periods will seem to have an overlapping End and Start time stamp, but the first(earliest in time) period should be interpreted to stop right before the End time stamp. This means the time periods are non-overlapping.
  • If a date or timestamp is not set it defaults to the C# DateTime value for UtcMin: 0001-01-01T00:00:00.000Z. The value of this constant is equivalent to 00:00:00.0000000 UTC, January 1, 0001, in the Gregorian calendar.
  • If a period is unbounded, end is represented as the C# DateTime value for UtcMax: 9999-12-31T23:59:58.999Z. The value of this constant is equivalent to 23:59:59.9999999 UTC, December 31, 9999 in the Gregorian calendar, exactly one 100-nanosecond tick before 00:00:00 UTC, January 1, 10000.
  • Some data have start and end-dates. For example: A metering point defines when it is/was associated to market price lists.
  • A default (empty) ID can be represented both using the empty GUID 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000 and null. A metering point tells it's connection state with a start and an end. etc.

Technical notes
